hypothesis: The upper candle shadow (high minus max of open/close) represents failed bullish attempts. Persistent upper shadows signal overhead selling pressure and a bearish short-term outlook.
The lower candle shadow (min of open/close minus low) represents rejected bearish attempts and buying support. Large lower shadows signal strong demand at price lows and bullish reversal potential.
formula: group_neutralize(trade_when(volume > adv20 * 0.65, rank(ts_decay_linear(min(open, close) - low, 5)), 0), subindustry)

hypothesis: Overnight price gaps normalized by dynamic 10-day return volatility represent pure dislocation signals. By applying a 75% liquidity gate and a smooth 6-day decay, we minimize turnover and maximize risk-adjusted payout.
Extreme price displacement from VWAP normalized by intraday range measures session stretch on high volume. Reversion captures fade to mean value.
Short-term cumulative return momentum normalized by dynamic 10-day return volatility identifies market-independent exhaustion points.
Comparing open position vs close position within daily high-low channel on large volume exposes early-session buyer traps that mean-revert.
formula: group_neutralize(trade_when(volume > adv20 * 0.7, -rank(ts_decay_linear(((close - low) - (open - low)) / (high - low + 0.001), 5)), 0), subindustry)

hypothesis: Correlation between returns and relative volume captures drying institutional liquidity. High correlation acts as a reversion signal.
Overnight price gap return minus active session intraday return, scaled by dynamic standard deviation, captures overnight sentiment excesses.
Daily return relative to its 10-day volatility, scaled by relative trading volume, identifies high-activity exhaustion extremes.
Standardized intraday high-to-low range signed by daily return captures volatility exhaustion on high-conviction days.
formula: group_neutralize(trade_when(volume > adv20 * 0.65, -rank(ts_decay_linear(((high - low) / (ts_mean(high - low, 20) + 0.001)) * returns, 5)), 0), subindustry)

hypothesis: Closing price deviation from 5-day moving average VWAP, standardized by 10-day price std dev, isolates reversion relative to rolling market cost basis.
Price deviations normalized by dynamic high-low spread capture extreme retail imbalances on high relative volume. Fading these imbalances yields strong risk-adjusted mean reversion.
Rolling correlation between intraday candle spread and volume isolates high-conviction institutional breakouts. Overbought climaxes on up-days act as strong reversion triggers.
formula: group_neutralize(trade_when(volume > adv20 * 0.7, -rank(ts_decay_linear(ts_corr(high - low, volume, 10) * returns, 5)), 0), subindustry)

hypothesis: Closing price distance from intraday VWAP, normalized by rolling 20-day return standard deviation, captures true price dislocation. Fading extreme stretch on liquid stocks produces high Sharpe.
formula: group_neutralize(trade_when(volume > adv20 * 0.65, rank(ts_decay_linear((vwap - close) / (ts_std_dev(returns, 20) * close + 0.001), 5)), 0), subindustry)

hypothesis: Stocks experiencing large short-term returns relative to their industry peers represent cross-sectional price stretch. These temporary imbalances reverse over a 4-day window.
Large overnight gaps relative to rolling 10-day active session high-low range represent pure retail sentiment peaks. Fading these overnight peaks captures gap exhaustion.
